text:
Columbus comes in with a 2-1 overtime win over Vegas, Adam Fantilli's power-play one-timer, but they're 2-3-0 in their last five and have been outscored 16-9 in that stretch. Philadelphia is 3-2-0 over the same span, though Saturday's 5-4 loss to Anaheim, after blowing a two-goal lead, ended a three-game winning streak. The Flyers are still without Travis Konecny and Owen Tippett (both on injured reserve), Rasmus Ristolainen is out too, and Emil Andrae returns to Philadelphia for the first time since leaving the Flyers after 107 games.

The chance numbers lean Columbus. At five on five, the Blue Jackets have taken 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, Philadelphia 38%. Our model sees a near coin flip anyway, 3.02 expected goals for CBJ and 2.88 for PHI. Philadelphia takes 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps feeding power plays. In net, projected starters Cam Talbot (CBJ) and Dan Vladar (PHI) are both slightly ahead of expectation this season. Vladar is also 12.74 goals saved above expected last season, while Talbot was at minus 13.67.

Matvei Michkov has nine points in his last ten games, and we have him at 29% to score. Fantilli sits at 29% too, and Trevor Zegras, on a four-game point streak, is 60% for a point. Our under-the-radar picks are Cole Sillinger (CBJ), a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately (36% for a point), and Porter Martone (PHI), who is 46% for a point with his ice time up since Konecny went down. Both are players to watch, not locks.
